newsitem.title: SPAIN: Thousands join Spain tribute to hanged ETA inmate.
newsitem.headline: Thousands join Spain tribute to hanged ETA inmate.

text.p: Some 4,000 people paid silent tribute on Tuesday to Juan Carlos Hernando, an ETA Basque separatist guerrilla inmate who was found hanged in a central Spanish jail on Sunday, police said.
The demonstration, organised by Hernando's family, started in a central square of his hometown in the northern Basque town of Arrigorriga, about 10 km (six miles) from Bilbao.
The group moved through the streets with a banner saying in the Basque language "Peli (nickname) we love you, justice and freedom are the road to peace".

The tribute to the ETA inmate, who was found hanged in his cell in an apparent suicide, comes days after Spaniards took to the streets in unprecedented numbers to protest against a brutal killing by the rebels. Officials had feared violent clashes between pro- and anti-ETA supporters.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people since 1968 when it began a campaign for an independent Basque state.

But the separatist rebel group went too far in the eyes of most Spaniards when it kidnapped a 29-year-old Spanish politician on July 10 and two days later carried out a threat to kill him as the country watched horrified and helpless.
Politicians in Arrigorriga blamed Hernando's death on the government's policy of dispersing ETA prisoners in small groups around the country to prevent them from plotting behind bars.
